subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity increase & overflow approach
messages:
From: Sara Wong <sara.wong@nimbus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity needs & overflow behavior

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal window is coming up in June and we need to lock in both committed Dedicated capacity and the overflow behavior for spikes. Quick background: we currently run a steady-state pool of 12x A100-equivalent GPUs with a mix of generation and a modest hosted fallback, and we expect product usage to grow ~40% year-over-year. Key asks from our side:

- Add reserved GPUs to cover baseline growth (we're targeting 18 reserved units)
- A clear overflow policy for peak traffic windows (max QPS spikes ~3-4x baseline for up to 30 minutes)
- A firm SLA for throughput during business hours and defined fallbacks when reserved pool saturates

Can you confirm what options Redwood supports during renewal: strictly hard caps on usage versus on-demand spillover to hosted capacity, how pricing would work for both, and any carriage/latency implications? We'd like to have concrete options and cost delta to present to procurement by mid-May.

Also include any proposed contract language changes (term, committed units, burst allowances). I’ve looped in Nathan (ops) who can share telemetry if you need numbers.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Wong
Head of Platform — Nimbus AI
[sara.wong@nimbus.ai]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Nathan Li <nathan.li@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-04-30T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity needs & overflow behavior

Sara — thanks for the clear summary. We can absolutely give you concrete paths for the renewal. High level options we typically present:

1) Reserved expansion + soft overflow (recommended for growth)
   - Commit to N additional dedicated GPUs for the contract term.
   - During transient spikes Redwood routes overflow to our hosted (shared) pool up to a configured percentage. Overflow is metered separately and billed at an on-demand rate.

2) Reserved expansion + hard cap (strict control)
   - Commit to the number you want; requests beyond that are throttled. Good for strict cost ceilings but may increase tail latency or error rates during spikes.

3) Hybrid with priority routing and guaranteed throughput windows
   - A subset of requests marked high-priority get routed to reserved pool with explicit throughput guarantees; lower-priority requests can spill to hosted or be queued.

I attached a one-page options summary and a proposed capacity schedule to start pricing. Can Rishi/Evelyn confirm technical feasibility and the rough price delta for option 1 vs 2? Also listing a suggested contract line for an automatic spillover cap (e.g., overflow capped at 60% of reserved baseline per 15-min window) so procurement can evaluate.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-min sync with procurement and ops next week.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: renewal_options_v1.pdf]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Wong <sara.wong@nimbus.ai>, Nathan Li <nathan.li@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus renewal — capacity ask details

Jordan / Evelyn — quick technical and commercial readout below. TL;DR: we can support both hard-cap and soft-overflow; recommend soft-overflow with controlled spill caps for Nimbus.

Technical notes:
- SKU recommendation: reserve 12x A100 + 6x H100 (or 18x H100 if they prefer single-family) depending on model mix. H100s save ~12-20% latency for 8k-token workloads but cost more.
- Throughput: a reserved pool sized to 18 H100-equivalents should handle baseline + 1.5x sustained growth with headroom for short spikes. For 3-4x spikes, we expect spillover to hosted pool to be required for most customers.
- Overflow mechanics: we can apply a configurable spill cap measured as additional capacity percent of the reserved pool per rolling 15-min window. When the cap is exceeded we have two policy options: 1) throttle lower-priority requests (hard cap behavior), or 2) continue to route to hosted pool but at higher metered rates with soft-exhaustion alarms.
- Latency/cold-start: routing to hosted pool may add 30-120 ms tail latency depending on model and region; KV cache misses impact costs for repeated prefixes.

Commercial recommendations:
- Option A (soft-overflow): commit to 18 reserved units, allow hosted spillover up to 60% of reserved capacity per 15-min window. Meter overflow at on-demand rate (suggested +35% over committed unit cost). Add a monthly overflow budget that auto-applies when exceeded to avoid surprise bills.
- Option B (hard-cap): commit to 18 reserved units; hard throttle beyond that. Lower unit cost vs Option A but with risk of failed requests during peaks.
- Pricing ballpark (monthly committed): 18x reserved A100-equivalent = $XX,XXX/mo list; overflow metered at $Y.ZZ per token-equivalent (we'll give line items in the quote).

Next steps: I can produce a precise quote by specifying model families and token mix per month (Nathan/Sara can provide). Also prepared a short SLA clause that defines throughput guarantees for business hours and fallback behavior when overflow is used.

Rishi
Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Proposed renewal structure and next steps (ND-7834)

Sara / Nathan — thanks for the patience and for sharing traffic signals. Summary of the recommended approach and next steps so procurement has a clean package: 

What we propose (recommended):
- Commit to 18 reserved GPU-equivalents for a 12-month renewal term (baseline covers projected growth).
- Soft overflow enabled: Redwood will route excess traffic to hosted pool up to 60% of reserved baseline per rolling 15-minute window. Overflow is metered at an on-demand uplift of +35% over the committed unit rate.
- Priority routing: Nimbus can flag up to 30% of requests as high-priority (business-critical routing) and those will be routed to reserved capacity first; lower-priority requests are eligible for spill to hosted capacity.
- SLA carve-outs: during overflow we guarantee 99.5% of high-priority tokens served within agreed latency; non-priority requests best-effort. We’ll attach the SLA bullets to the contract.

Commercials / attachments:
- Attached: renewal_options_v1.pdf, proposed_capacity_schedule.xlsx, nd7834_sla_draft.pdf
- Link to the draft DocuSign for signature when Nimbus is ready: https://docusign.com/nd7834/sign

Requested next steps:
1) Nathan — share monthly token mix so Rishi can finalize line-item pricing (link to Drive provided).
2) Sara — confirm that the soft-overflow cap (60% per 15-min window) is acceptable to procurement. If not, we can re-run with 30% cap (lower exposure, lower overflow spend).
3) Once commercials are agreed we’ll issue a contract amendment and DocuSign envelope for signatures.

If you want a short (20–30 min) exec call to walk procurement through the tradeoffs I can set that up.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
